label: rem:swampland-no-global-symmetry
title: Swampland correspondence: observability and the absence of global symmetries
html:
The observability axiom (quantum observable universe, condition ii) requires:

  \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0.

The adjoint object carries no invariant section. This provides the categorical form of a foundational Swampland criterion.

The Swampland statement. A consistent theory of quantum gravity admits no exact global symmetry [banks-seiberg2011]. In holographic settings, this is established rather than conjectural [harlow-ooguri2021]. A global symmetry would act on the matter content while commuting with every local observable. This leaves a sector that no measurement can reach.

QOU translation. The vanishing \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0 equates to the vanishing of the zeroth adjoint cohomology H^0_G(\mathrm{Ad}(A)) . The Lie algebra of \mathrm{Aut}^{\otimes}(\tau) is exactly \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)). The axiom therefore excludes any infinitesimal automorphism of the fibre functor \tau that acts trivially on every observable. This precisely forbids a decoupled global symmetry. Every internal degree of freedom is gauge-accessible to measurement.

Scope. The correspondence is structural. The Swampland statement constrains dynamical gravity based on black-hole physics. Here, the same exclusion is imposed as a categorical axiom and discharged in Lean as \mathrm{Subsingleton}\bigl((\mathbf{1}_{\mathbf{C}}) \to \mathrm{Ad}(A)\bigr). The framework does not derive the no-global-symmetry principle of quantum gravity. It internalises the same structural content.
